q: Does the pINV/pWR100 virulence megaplasmid (ipa/mxi-spa T3SS + ipaH effector arsenal) undergo detectable replication drift, deletion, or IS-mediated rearrangement across long-term-passaged M90T laboratory subclones held in different labs worldwide, and does that drift correlate with silent loss of invasion phenotype in cell-culture models?
basis: Cervantes-Rivera et al. 2020 (this paper, BMC Genomics 21:285) note that pWR100 (232,195 bp) carries the complete Shigella virulence apparatus and that the field had previously relied on the independently sequenced pWR501 (AF348706) from a different M90T lineage. The independently reproduced VFDB scan here shows 64 plasmid VF genes on NZ_CP037924.1 and PlasmidFinder types it IncFII_1 --- but only this Umeå isolate at a single time-point. The paper itself is a single-lab, single-time-point complete assembly; it does not survey the M90T sublineage tree that decades of pathogenesis labs have propagated.
next_steps: Assemble a multi-lab M90T sublineage panel (Sansonetti, Puhar/Umeå, ATCC, DSMZ, LMG, ETH-Zurich, and other holders that have re-deposited M90T-like assemblies since 2020). Run PacBio HiFi or Nanopore R10 on each subclone. For each: (1) compare pWR100 length, replicon count, and IS-mediated boundary breakpoints; (2) diff ipa/mxi/spa/ipg/osp/ipaH inventories against the Cervantes-Rivera 5a M90T reference; (3) correlate any plasmid-content deltas with published invasion-assay phenotypes for that specific sublineage. Publish a pWR100-drift atlas as a community reference.

q: The Cervantes-Rivera assembly reinforces the well-known Shigella-inside-Escherichia phylogeny (fastANI 97.8% to E. coli K12 vs 99.93% to S. flexneri 5b 8401): what does a chromosome-resolved, IS-element-aware pan-genome of complete S. flexneri + E. coli complete assemblies say about whether the current Shigella genus should be formally reclassified as Escherichia (pseudo-Escherichia lineages), and how much of the 'Shigella-specific' gene content is really IS-mediated pseudogenization of E. coli ancestral genes vs bona fide HGT?
basis: This replication measured fastANI 97.808% to E. coli K12 MG1655 vs 99.933% to S. flexneri 5b 8401 --- consistent with the long-standing polyphyletic-Shigella-within-E.coli literature. The paper itself frames M90T as a Shigella-specific reference while the ANI evidence and the 757-pseudogene, ~600-IS-transposase load (this replication) are the hallmarks of Shigella-style reductive evolution FROM an E. coli ancestor. No formal reclassification decision has been made by NCBI/ICSP.
next_steps: Build a complete-only (no-scaffold) pan-genome across all deposited S. flexneri serotypes (2a/5a/5b/6/X/Y), S. sonnei, S. dysenteriae, S. boydii, and a stratified E. coli sample (K12, EAEC, EIEC O124, EHEC O157, ETEC, ExPEC, commensal). Use PPanGGOLiN or Panaroo with IS-element masking (ISEScan) before core-genome definition. Publish (a) an IS-aware core-genome tree, (b) a pseudogene-corrected core-gene tree, (c) a formal ANI/dDDH matrix, and (d) a nomenclature proposal to ICSP/List of Prokaryotic Names WITH Standing to reclassify Shigella spp. as Escherichia.

q: Given the Cervantes-Rivera closed-genome PGAP annotation of M90T (5,003 CDS, 102 tRNA, 22 rRNA, 757 pseudogene, ~600 IS transposases in this independent re-parse), how many biologically real small RNAs, leaderless small ORFs (<50 aa), and previously-missed T3SS-secreted effectors are present in M90T that PGAP misses, and what fraction of the paper's 6,723 dRNA-seq primary TSS actually correspond to unannotated small-transcript features?
basis: The paper's dRNA-seq TSS map (6,723 primary + 7,328 secondary --- claim C9 in this replication, not re-run) far exceeds what a 5,003-CDS annotation can naturally originate, which strongly implies that a substantial fraction of TSS are intergenic / novel-sRNA / small-ORF / anti-sense. The paper does light integration with RegulonDB/RSAT but does not systematically re-annotate M90T against modern small-ORF callers (Ribo-seq-aware) or against curated Shigella/E.coli sRNA catalogs (BSRD, RegulonDB v11).
next_steps: Re-analyse PRJNA510559 dRNA-seq raw reads with TSSpredator + ANNOgesic; overlay against Ribo-seq if available (or new Ribo-seq on M90T); systematically call sORFs with DeepRibo / smORFer / RiboTISH; cross-reference against BSRD / sRNAdb / RegulonDB small-RNA annotations. Deposit an M90T v2 annotation as a community amendment to GCF_004799585.1 and negotiate with NCBI for an updated PGAP re-annotation run.

q: How does the SfII/SfV/SfX/Sf6 O-antigen serotype-conversion bacteriophage repertoire and its integration-site diversity vary across a contemporary global S. flexneri clinical panel, and does the mobile-element load carried by these prophages (beyond the O-antigen glycosyltransferase / acetyltransferase itself) shape vaccine-antigen selection, cross-serotype protection, and emergence of novel serotypes?
basis: The Cervantes-Rivera 2020 M90T assembly is serotype 5a, providing a modern reference for one specific serotype. The paper implicitly frames M90T as one serotype within a serotype-variable species. Global public-health data show S. flexneri serotype prevalence shifting (2a and 3a historically dominant, 1c/1b rising, novel serotypes documented) but the modern complete-assembly panel across serotypes remains thin.
next_steps: Collect a global geographically- and temporally-stratified panel of ~200 recent S. flexneri clinical isolates (Africa, South Asia, Latin America 2020-2026), long-read (Nanopore R10 or PacBio HiFi) sequence to closure, and specifically catalog: (1) SfII/SfV/SfX/Sf6/other O-antigen phages, integration sites, and cargo genes beyond the glycosyltransferase; (2) LPS-modification loci (gtrA/B/C, oac); (3) O-antigen structural-locus (wzy/wzx/rfb) sequence diversity. Feed into GSK/Institut Pasteur/Bharat Biotech Shigella-vaccine antigen-selection pipelines; publish a phage-inclusive O-antigen typing scheme.

q: What is the full anti-phage-defense-island and CRISPR-Cas inventory (Type I-E, retrons, CBASS, DSR, Gabija, Thoeris, Hachiman, Wadjet, etc.) across complete S. flexneri assemblies (including M90T), and does the observed defense-system landscape predict the susceptibility of specific S. flexneri lineages to a rationally curated shigellosis phage-therapy cocktail?
basis: The Cervantes-Rivera 2020 complete M90T genome (this replication verified 4,596,714 bp chromosome + pWR100, deposited PGAP annotation) is the natural substrate for a modern defense-island scan --- but the paper itself does not report a systematic anti-phage-defense catalog (defense-island discovery post-dates the paper: DefenseFinder 2022, PADLOC 2022, Doron et al. 2018 lineage). Phage-therapy interest in shigellosis is rising given AMR trends, but the M90T defense landscape has not been mapped against modern databases.
next_steps: Run DefenseFinder + PADLOC + CRISPRCasFinder v4 on the deposited GCF_004799585.1 assembly to catalog M90T's defense inventory. Extend to the full complete-only S. flexneri panel (serotypes 2a/5a/5b/6/X/Y). Cross-reference against curated Shigella-phage collections (Sf6, Sf24, phage-therapy candidates from Adaptive Phage Therapeutics / Locus / GEIS Georgia collection). Design an in-vitro receptor-and-defense-profile challenge matrix: predict phage-cocktail effectiveness per lineage; publish a Shigella-phage-therapy compatibility atlas anchored on complete-genome-derived defense catalogs.
